answer: Each identity seals a unique 2 GB replica, encoded with slow Sloth-style keyed encoding bound to its public key, and the replica root becomes a vertex in a registry Merkle DAG. Verifiers then demand random 4 KB openings within 300 ms, so the data must sit on local SSD, since glacier storage takes hours to thaw. A failed opening slashes a 20 token bond immediately. Ten thousand fakes cost an attacker 20 TB of NVMe near $1,800, about 55,000 encoding core-hours near $2,200, and 200,000 bonded tokens at risk. One surprise audit splits such a swarm like a hammer on a walnut.
